title: GAP Waiver Plus 150 Exclusions: Force-Placed Premiums Once a Placement Ends
content:
For the GAP Waiver Addenda Plus 150 excluded total, the force-placed premiums enter as the placed-premium part. That part is net of refunds credited or, where the proof's coverage starts inside the latest billing period, net of the refund due. The figures come from the contract's Collateral Protection Insurance tracking record.

**How the placement ended, and the resulting placed-premium part**

- **Refunds of those premiums were credited back to the contract balance.** The part is the premiums added less the refunds credited.
- **No refund credited, and the coverage starts inside the latest billing period.** This applies when the latest accepted proof of insurance was reviewed on or after the billing date of the latest premium added, and its policy effective date falls within that premium's billing period. The part is the premiums added less that latest premium's share for the days of its billing period from the proof's policy effective date on. The share is the premium times those days divided by the days of its billing period, both counted inclusive, rounded half-up to the cent. It is the whole refund the collateral protection terms leave due when the proof's coverage starts inside the latest billing period.
- **Any other ending.** This includes a proof whose coverage starts before the latest billing period while its refund is not yet credited. The premiums added enter without any reduction.

**Definitions.**

- The latest premium added is the force-placed premium whose billing period starts latest, whatever its billing date. A backdated placement bills two or more premiums on one day, while no two premiums share a billing period.
- The latest accepted proof is the accepted proof with the latest review date. Where two accepted proofs were reviewed on that date, the one recorded first counts.

*Hypothetical case.* A 31-day latest billing period carries a premium of 124.00, and an accepted proof shows coverage from day 16. Days 16 to 31 inclusive are 16 days, so the share is 124.00 times 16 divided by 31, which is 64.00.
